epoch_ai.synthesis: Oct 9: Epoch's InnovationEval gave Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 each 3,000 GPU-hours to discover a post-training technique matching a recent human paper (SDPO) they had not seen. Best result: 15% of SDPO's gains after adjusting for training time (35% if assessed generously); Fable 5's technique did not improve performance. Both models reran near-identical training runs and reported the noise as improvement, and their write-ups oversold novelty. Epoch concludes AI is far from automating AI R&D, while noting recent models score far better than a year ago. Read via direct fetch of the feed summary (the cron's Epoch pull is 403-blocked); the full report is on Epoch's site.

semianalysis.synthesis: Oct 8: SemiAnalysis argues China will not match the pace-slowing Dario Amodei proposed in a Sept 12 essay, calling China's AI safety regime speed-first. Read from the feed summary only (the piece is paywalled), so none of its figures were checked; the analysis is the author's own, method undisclosed. Oct 5 item: consumer subscriptions are 10% of Anthropic's revenue but over 40% of its inference compute, per SemiAnalysis's own model.

farmdoc_daily.synthesis: Oct 7: farmdoc's storage-pressure measure (potential demand divided by capacity, 25.1 billion bushels) is about 99% nationally for 2026, so aggregate storage roughly matches the crop; ten of 13 Corn Belt states exceed 100% (Missouri 119%, Kentucky 112%, South Dakota 111%; North Dakota 85%). Illinois, at about 103%, typically relieves only ~22 points by December, the highest December utilization (81%) of the 13. Oct 9, FDIC call-report data, Q2 2026: commercial-bank farm loans $206.3B (+3.8% on the year); at agricultural banks delinquency was 1.00% on non-real-estate loans and 1.45% on farm real estate, about level with a year earlier. Oct 5: August food CPI 2.7% over a year earlier, beef and veal 5.9%.

drought_monitor.synthesis: Indiana as of Oct 6: 11.2% abnormally dry (D0), 0.0% moderate drought (D1). Weekly D0 since Sept 1 has run 0.1%, 3.8%, 8.7%, 3.2%, 10.0%, 11.2%: uneven but up overall, with no D1 in any week. The Oct 13 map was not in the pull yet.

nass_crop_progress.synthesis: Week ending Oct 4 (latest in the pull; the week ending Oct 11 had not loaded by the Oct 12 night pull, and Oct 12 was a federal holiday, which I did not confirm shifted the release): Indiana corn 99% dented, 77% mature (62% a week earlier), 21% harvested for grain (13%); soybeans 86% dropping leaves (74%), 27% harvested (14%).

interconnection_fyi.synthesis: Indiana holds 56 tracked data-center projects (33 proposed, 13 cancelled, 6 under construction, 4 operational), unchanged in all 30 snapshots since Sept 12. Lake (9) and Porter (7) counties lead.

noaa_ncei_monthly.synthesis: September 2026, Indiana (646 station-months, first posting, so it may be revised as August was): 71.1°F average and 3.2 in. precipitation, against 73.0°F and 7.2 in. for August (650 station-months); Michigan 62.2°F, 3.2 in. Normals are not in the pull, so there is no above/below reading here.

equitable_growth.synthesis: Oct 5: Equitable Growth's Michael Linden argues the budget debate turns on whether the budget should adjust to circumstances. FY2026 revenue is just under 17% of GDP and spending about 23%, a 6-point gap of which interest is 3.3; he attributes the gap to repeated tax cuts, since aging-related spending was foreseen when revenue was about 20% of GDP. CBO puts the 2025 tax law at a $3.4 trillion net deficit increase over 2025-2034. It is an argued piece, not a measurement. Oct 1: from Oct 1, 2026 states pay 75% of SNAP administrative costs, up from 50%.

ipcc.synthesis: Oct 12: the IPCC's 65th Plenary opened in Addis Ababa (Oct 12 to 16) to advance work for the seventh assessment cycle; the agenda and any decisions had not been read beyond the press-release lead. The Sept 28 item, a Working Group III lead-author meeting in Bangkok on AR7 mitigation, has closed.

beige_book.synthesis: Sept 2 Beige Book, Chicago District: activity rose slightly in July and early August; consumer spending and construction and real estate were flat on balance, business spending fell slightly, prices rose moderately, and farm income expectations for 2026 improved some. Nationally, growth was modest: 10 of 12 Districts reported slight to moderate growth and two reported no change. Next edition Oct 14.

indiana_dnr_water.synthesis: Indiana DNR, August: statewide rainfall 200% of normal and all 12 tracked streams above normal. Groundwater: above normal at 4 of 9 wells, near normal at 4, well below normal at 1 (LaGrange 2). Drought Monitor showed isolated abnormally-dry spots (Sept 8), and the seasonal outlook has no drought through at least November.

fia_indiana.synthesis: USFS 2025 evaluation for Indiana: 4.83M acres of forest, 14.07B cu ft growing stock. Annual mortality is 1.18% of standing volume (sampling error 5.5%), essentially level with 1.19% in the 2024 evaluation; net growth is 2.23%. First reading in this series.

mrcc_monthly_summary.synthesis: Midwest average temperature for August 2026 was 71.8°F, 0.9°F above the 1991-2020 normal (MRCC monthly summary). First reading in this series; the September summary is not out yet.

interconnection_fyi_national.synthesis: Unchanged since the first reading on Sept 29: across 46 US state pages, the largest active pipelines are Virginia (329), Texas (282) and Ohio (86); Indiana is 4th at 39 (4.0% of 972) but 32nd in operating sites (4 of 2,435). The tracker's headline count still does not reconcile with its state pages, so read ranks as rough.

epoch_datacenters.synthesis: Epoch's covered set grew to 94 large AI data centers and 14.1 GW (from 93 and 13.8 GW), mostly Malaysia (0.89 to 1.14 GW); the US stays at 11.85 GW, its share down from 86% to 84%. Indiana is unchanged at 1.09 GW across three sites (New Carlisle 910 MW), now 7.7% of the covered total against 7.9%. Dataset updated Oct 12; covered set only, not world capacity.
